why: Both describe a room specifying its mark, one settling its look and one circulating coordinates or how-to, and they co-occur whenever a design thread hands placers something to follow, so the boundary is easy to cross.

why.T3-004: The bulk of the concepts work out the MIT mark's look — three-pixel versus one-pixel letters, two-pixel whitespace, and adding and completing the red dot — and correct detail against the plan; the coordinate setting is subordinate to settling the design.

why.T3-010: Neighbouring rooms (WPI, r/farmcarrots, the orange banner, McGill) settle lines, regions and shifts of space around the MIT logo — reciprocal build offers, an alternative region suggested, and a birb resized to fit without overwriting — no fight is ended, so borders not truce.

why.T3-004: An unplanned pink tongue is taken into Pusheen's design ('wasn't in the original plan but it's amazing and I'm going to keep it'), a change to the mark's look adopted and defended; this is settling the design rather than repairing damage or routing posts.

why.T3-005: Calls to save Pusheen, naming the Dutch attack, warning of vandalism, and deciding to draw her over the Dutch flag are an attack on the work and the room's answer, not a plea or a repair.

why.T3-009: A lone 'Nice work!' marks the others' logo work as finished and good, celebrating an achieved work rather than cheering builders while a build goes on.

why.T3-045: The exchange argues priority and theft over the Jets logo — 'the logo that you stole from us' — an accusation of stealing after the Jets' area was wiped, which is the priority/stealing dispute rather than a taunt or a rebuild.

why.T3-041: After the logo is done, the room proposes adding Tim the Beaver beside it — a second picture added to the existing work ('let's do a whole Tim') — then weighs the fight with the orange banner, which is extension rather than a first proposal.

why.T3-010: r/cirkeltrek brings its plan to expand left into r/pusheen for comment — a neighbouring room settling space with a neighbour before moving, not pleading with attackers.

why.T3-009: Celebrating Pusheen reborn and part of the final canvas, with relief the canvas did not end earlier — the room's finished work marked as achieved, not a rival victory or an announcement of a mark still being placed.

why.T3-005: Asking people to defend the old or small MIT logo against vandalism, culminating in coordinates and a javascript defence method — direct calls and automated help are both the room answering attacks.
Calls for more power and to fight back as r/masseffect and r/nyjets draw over or overrun the heart — an attack under way and the room's rally to hold the line.
The same mobilisation passages repeated: calls to save Pusheen, the Dutch attack named, and drawing her over the Dutch flag — defending the work against attackers.

why.T3-022: After failed saving, friends quietly bring Pusheen back at a new spot ('down at the bottom of the map') — the work restarted elsewhere after being lost; the surrounding cleanup is a subordinate upkeep aspect.
The overpowered heart is moved to new coordinates after defeat — 'the call's made we're moving', a different location found when Mass Effect overran the old spot.
why.T3-070: Separately, the member supplies a semi-transparent guide and a work link for the relocated heart, directions placers need that the relocation concept does not carry.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-022's gate reaches the heart being overpowered and moved to new coordinates but not the member supplying a semi-transparent guide and a work link so placers can rebuild the relocated heart; those circulating-how-to concepts have no home in the relocation theme.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0116243 (semi-transparent guide for the new heart) and C1209692 (direct link to where the heart is being drawn and what is attempted) post what placers need to reproduce the work.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-070; dropping it loses the guide and work link for the new heart and leaves only the fact of the move.
